summary.title: About Me
summary.summaryText:
My name is Artemiy, I am a Manual QA Engineer with almost three years of experience. My main focus is backend and API testing, but I also worked with UI, checking responsiveness, cross-browser compatibility, and data display correctness.

I started my career at Stepik, where I worked for two and a half years and grew from a junior to a middle-level QA. Stepik is a large online education platform with a microservice architecture: the backend was implemented with Django/Python, PostgreSQL was used as the main database, Redis and RabbitMQ were used for caching and queues, and the frontend was built with React.

Within the project, I tested the student’s personal account, covering registration, authorization, password recovery, profile editing, avatar uploads. Most of my work was focused on API testing with Postman and Swagger: I tested endpoints, performed positive and negative checks, validated JSON structures, and verified status codes. To ensure data correctness, I used SQL queries to PostgreSQL and compared database values with frontend output.

In addition to API testing, I worked on courses and assignments: checking access, assignment flow, automated code validation, and the progress system with deadlines and certificates. On the frontend side, I verified cross-browser support and responsive design, as well as client-side form validation. The team worked under Scrum methodology with two-week sprints. Tasks were managed in Jira, documentation was kept in Confluence, and regression testing was carried out after each release.

After that, I joined the Ipsilon project at Saratov State University. It is a distance learning system where I participated in redesign, modernization, and platform updates. The architecture included a Ruby on Rails backend with REST API, PostgreSQL as the main database, Redis for caching and sessions, and React on the frontend.

Since the team was small, with only three QA engineers, I covered the full testing cycle: verifying APIs for grade books, exam schedules, student personal accounts, and course enrollment. I worked less with the frontend. The workflow was organized under Kanban, all bugs and tasks were tracked in Jira. This project gave me valuable experience as a versatile QA, covering the product end-to-end — from API and database to the user interface.

Overall, my main focus is backend and API testing, but I always aim to see the product as a whole. I am skilled at working with databases, analyzing logs, testing interfaces, writing test documentation, and adapting to both large Scrum teams and smaller Kanban setups. I am interested in projects with complex architecture and integrations where I can dive deeper into logic and data validation.
strengths: Attention to detail and focus on product quality
Experienced in designing test cases, checklists, and bug reports
Able to quickly understand business logic and system requirements
Proactive in identifying risks and edge cases
Team-oriented, but capable of independent decision-making
Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills
